parents.title: Even-function redundancy in the Young boundary equation

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The eigenvalue description forgets part of the representation data. The arbitrary even component identifies the kernel of this projection and makes clear why saddle equivalence alone cannot reconstruct a dominant Young profile uniquely.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The character action and boundary equation connect h to rho while the even-function freedom measures information lost in passing from Young data to the eigenvalue marginal.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span rewrites the character action in theta and rho and uses evenness of rho to show invariance under adding any even f(theta) to h(theta). It concludes that multiple Young distributions related by this shift correspond to the same eigenvalue density and inserts f into the generic boundary equation. It explicitly defers the phase-space restriction on this redundancy.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Rewriting the character action in theta and rho shows an h-dependent term whose pairing with even rho leaves the action unchanged under h(theta) to h(theta)+f(theta) for even f. The boundary equation therefore contains an arbitrary even function.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The source later restricts this freedom using constant-density droplet topology, but this unit does not eliminate it. Equal action and equal rho do not imply a unique Young distribution. The nonuniqueness conclusion is prose-clear; the displayed action and exact boundary coefficients are extraction-sensitive. Interpreting the even-function freedom as information lost when passing to the eigenvalue marginal is a precise reading of the invariance. The candidate correctly distinguishes equal action/equal rho from uniqueness of the Young profile. The exact action and boundary coefficients are extraction-sensitive, but the invariance and nonuniqueness are prose-explicit.

parents.title: No-gap and multi-gap topology fix boundary separation

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Topology supplies information absent from the eigenvalue saddle: it selects the allowed shape class and converts density into boundary thickness. It constrains the redundancy without necessarily specifying the absolute placement of both multi-gap boundaries.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The constant-density droplet, its boundary roots h_±, and their separation bridge eigenvalue density to phase-space geometry and candidate Young data.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: For a no-gap phase, the span gives boundary roots 0 and h_+(theta)=2*pi*rho(theta), with S=2*pi*rho and f=pi*rho. For a multi-gap phase, it gives two nonzero roots whose separation is 2*pi*rho and again obtains f=pi*rho. It explicitly defers the complete Young-distribution construction and invokes theta=pi*u(h) only as the subsequent identification.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: For a no-gap phase the boundary equation is constrained to roots 0 and h_+(theta)=2 pi rho(theta), giving S=2 pi rho and f=pi rho. For a multi-gap phase, roots h_+ and h_- obey h_+-h_-=2 pi rho, again fixing f=pi rho.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The source defers complete Young-distribution construction and invokes theta=pi u(h) afterward. No uniqueness theorem or full dominant-representation classification is provided, and exact factors remain equation-sensitive. The qualitative no-gap/multi-gap distinction and separation rule are clear; exact polynomial boundary formulas should be scan-checked. Reading topology as fixing boundary thickness from the eigenvalue density is a direct interpretation of the root-separation equations. The candidate appropriately says this constrains the redundancy without turning it into a uniqueness theorem for full dominant representations. The qualitative no-gap/multi-gap cases are clear; exact polynomial factors and one extracted root phrase require scan checking.

parents.title: One spiky density supports multiple normalized Young representations

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: For the invoked no-gap identification, the boundary reduces to h = 2*pi*rho(theta). Because the plotted density is not one-to-one, inversion must be restricted to monotone sectors, producing multiple branchwise Young densities for the same eigenvalue density. Constant low-h completions and normalization constrain each branch, but normalization does not select a unique representation and the examples do not classify all branches.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: It treats branch identity as information lost by globally inverting a non-injective boundary and explains why local monotone inversion plus normalization creates structural multiplicity rather than uniqueness.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after removing the external claim about the identification's proof status; the branch-splitting mechanism and its nonuniqueness limit are explicit and mathematically substantive.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span gives the reduced boundary, explicitly says a fixed h can have several theta values, constructs example representations sector by sector, fixes constants using the unit-integral condition, and concludes that multiple U(N) representations extremize the character and partition function for one eigenvalue distribution.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Multiplicity is established in the span conditional on the theta = pi*u(h) identification it invokes. Exact intervals, constants, and figure geometry are extraction- and figure-sensitive, so the displayed examples are not promoted to a complete classification.

parents.title: Lagrange-multiplier route to theta=pi*u(h)

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The appendix tests compatibility of theta = pi*u(h) with stated constraints rather than deriving it uniquely. It adds a Lagrange multiplier, factorizes positive h as gamma*gamma, varies to connect theta, mu, and -partial x/partial h = u(h), and selects mu = pi*sign(theta) to recover the desired relation. That particular choice is not shown to be forced, and the initial integral constraint is not shown to imply pointwise evenness of h in theta.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: It recasts the calculation as a constraint-compatibility witness and audits two missing implications—global integral to pointwise parity and admissible multiplier family to a unique selected multiplier—thereby locating the remaining proof burden.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after applying the critic's scope correction: the record retains the supported mechanism and internal gaps while removing the outside claim that another span labels the result heuristic and unproved.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span displays the integral constraint, asserts evenness, introduces the multiplier and positive factorization, gives the variational relation and u definition, imposes oddness and a bound on mu, and chooses the sign-dependent multiplier to obtain pi*u(h) = theta.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The described variational strategy is internal to the span, but uniqueness and forced selection are not established. Reciprocals, signs, the mu bound, and the final pi factor are extraction-sensitive and require scan verification; no external statement about the main text is used.
